I am a statistician at Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University in Bauchi, Nigeria, where
I have worked in the Academic Planning & Quality Assurance unit since 2015 —
building the institutional databases that sixty-odd departments report into, and
advising the research projects that pass through them. Since 2017 I have also run
Frequently Bayesian Data Analytics, an independent consultancy doing much the same
work for clients in public health, finance and academia.

My MSc in Statistics is from ATBU and my BSc from the University of Maiduguri,
finishing in the top two of my class in both. The methods I reach for most are Bayesian
inference, survival analysis, spatial and geo-additive modelling, and time series
forecasting — usually on survey or health data, where the answer worth reporting is
an interval rather than a number.

This site is where I check that work instead of assuming it. A simulation that
disagrees with what I expected is the most useful thing I can publish, so most of
what is here is written to be run again rather than read once.

## Chess

I play as `BayesianRules` on both [Chess.com](https://www.chess.com/member/BayesianRules)
and [Lichess](https://lichess.org/@/BayesianRules), and have peaked at 2000 in
rapid and 2000 in blitz. It is the one place I get to reason about an opponent's
uncertainty rather than a distribution's, which turns out to be less of a change
of subject than it sounds.

## What this site is built on

Posts are written in Quarto and executed locally in one of two engines — R
4.5.2 via knitr, or Python 3.12 via Jupyter — chosen per post rather than per
site. Interactive figures are client-side (plotly, ggiraph, Vega-Lite), so
there is no server behind this page and nothing to go down.

## Why the numbers do not change

Every post's executed output is cached and committed alongside its source when
the post is published. Re-rendering the site replays that cache instead of
re-running the code. A package upgrade three years from now cannot silently
change a figure that was published today; changing a published result requires
editing the post, which is a visible act.

The source for the whole site, cache included, is on
[GitHub](https://github.com/batestguy/QuartoWebsite-blog-others).
